hero_lede: Booking, payment, consultations, privacy, and when online care is not the right route. Can't find what you need? Drop us a line.
stuck_h2_pre: Not the question you came with?
g1_q1: How do I book an online consultation?
g1_a1: Choose your country, select a service, pick a clinician and open time slot, then complete the patient details and checkout steps.
g1_q2: Can I choose the doctor before I book?
g1_a2: Yes. Doctor profiles show the clinician's registration details, specialties, languages, and bookable services where available.
g1_q3: Are appointments guaranteed for the same day?
g1_a3: No. Appointment times depend on clinician availability, country coverage, and the selected service. Open slots are shown during booking.
g2_q1: Can the doctor issue a prescription, referral, or certificate?
g2_a1: Where clinically appropriate, the treating doctor can issue next steps such as a prescription, referral, or certificate. These are never guaranteed before assessment.
g2_q2: Is online care suitable for emergencies?
g2_a2: No. Online consultations are not emergency care. If you need urgent help, call 112 or your local emergency number.
g3_a1: Global Health handles personal data under GDPR principles and collects the details needed to provide the service. You can read more in the privacy policy.
g3_q2: Will my consultation notes be available after the appointment?
g3_a2: Clinical notes or follow-up guidance may be shared after the consultation where appropriate for the service and country workflow.
g4_q1: When do I see the price?
g4_a1: Service prices are shown before booking and checkout. Final availability and payment options depend on the selected country and service.
g4_q2: Do I need a subscription or wellness plan?
g4_a2: No. The public site is currently built around pay-per-consultation and service-based bookings, not bundled wellness plans.
